labels.reason: Bounded NUL-terminated scan_id string scan (breaks on ' '/'\0', os_strchr-bounded) - matches confirmed 'ARR30-C on provably-bounded NUL-terminated string scan' pattern
atoi(pos) result stored with no error/range check beyond the separate count bound
same unchecked atoi() conversion, no error detection
Fixed-size int scan_id[MAX_SCAN_ID] array, no getenv/putenv anywhere in function - matches confirmed ENV01-C wholesale misfire pattern
'pos' is a generically-named local reused across many independent os_strstr assignments in this large function; no single value is actually used with both bitwise and arithmetic ops
!!atoi(pos+8) boolean-coerced but underlying atoi() overflow/error still undetected; literal ERR07-C violation
!!atoi(pos+15) boolean-coerced, still no error detection per rule text
Outer 'ssid ' parse loop terminates via NUL/space-bounded os_strchr traversal - matches confirmed bounded-NUL-scan ARR30-C FP pattern (variable misattributed as 'end' but same root cause)
Inner `while (*end) {... break; end++;}` scan is explicitly NUL/space-terminated - bounded, matches confirmed pattern
`(end - pos) & 0x01` parity check immediately followed by `end - pos > ...` comparison on the same subexpression - matches confirmed 'parity-check idiom' INT14-C stylistic-pedantry FP pattern

os_memcpy(..., scan_id, scan_id_count * sizeof(int)) copies exactly the scan_id_count elements scan_id_list_parse populated (scan_id_count starts at 0 and is only incremented as elements are written) - never reads past initialized data
wpa_msg args are MAC2STR(dst/src/bssid), pure side-effect-free macro reads - matches confirmed EXP30-C macro-logging-arg FP pattern
`len = os_strlen(param); if (len & 1) return -1; len /= 2;` - hex-string-length parity-check-then-arithmetic idiom, matches confirmed INT14-C stylistic FP pattern
Same hex-length parity-check-then-divide idiom as 9723 - confirmed FP pattern

event.rx_mgmt is the only member this function ever writes to this fresh memset union; 'channel_list_changed' write comes from an unrelated function/branch - matches confirmed EXP39-C cross-function/cross-branch union conflation FP pattern
res = os_zalloc(sizeof(*res) + ...) - sizeof(*res) is compile-time, not a dereference of the not-yet-assigned pointer - matches confirmed sizeof(*ptr) FP idiom
res->flags = strtol(...) return value never checked (no errno/endptr validation) in this DRIVER_EVENT test-string parser
errno not reset before strtol call

`*pos++ = '\0';` both sides char, no widening conversion - matches confirmed STR34-C char-to-char-assignment FP pattern

req_ies: classic reassign-then-free idiom - wpabuf_free(req_ies) at 'fail:' only ever targets req_ies's current (possibly still-NULL) value since every loop-body free already preceded a fresh reassignment; matches confirmed 'MEM31-C misfired on reassign-then-free local-variable-reuse idiom' pattern (tls_openssl_ocsp.c precedent)
resp_ies: same reassign-then-free idiom as req_ies
`*param++ = '\0';` char-to-char, no widening - matches confirmed STR34-C FP pattern

event.freq_range is the only member this AVOID_FREQUENCIES branch touches on this fresh memset union; 'channel_list_changed' is written only in a mutually-exclusive sibling branch of the same if/else-if chain that can never execute together - union-conflation/mutually-exclusive-branch FP

os_free(event.freq_range.range) is the actual (first) free of this branch's allocation; sqc appears to be crediting a free from a different, mutually-exclusive branch of the same if/else-if chain as having already run - same root cause as the confirmed mutually-exclusive-branch free-tracking FP family
`len = os_strlen(pos); if (len & 1) return -1; len /= 2;` - confirmed hex-length parity-check idiom
os_free(buf) where buf may be NULL (malloc failed) is standard-guaranteed safe - matches confirmed 'EXP34-C flags os_free(NULL) as unchecked deref' FP pattern
ipv4_hdr_checksum(const void *buf, size_t len) is the idiomatic ptr+len pair - matches confirmed API05-C FP pattern
sum uses >>, &, += as the standard IP-header-checksum fold algorithm - deliberate, well-known idiom, matches confirmed INT14-C stylistic-pedantry-mismatch pattern
wpas_data_test_rx(..., const u8 *buf, size_t len) is the idiomatic ptr+len pair - matches confirmed API05-C FP pattern
`len < sizeof(*eth) + sizeof(ip)` - sizeof(*eth) on not-yet-assigned 'eth' is compile-time only, not a dereference - matches confirmed sizeof(*ptr) FP idiom

`&buf[sizeof(*eth)+sizeof(ip)]` on `const u8 *buf` (1-byte pointee) is ordinary byte-pointer offset arithmetic, scale factor 1 - matches confirmed 'ARR39-C misfire on 1-byte-pointee sizeof offset' FP pattern

Loop bound `ntohs(ip.ip_len) - sizeof(ip)` is a size_t/integer subtraction used as a for-loop bound, not scaled pointer arithmetic - message mischaracterizes the real defect (captured separately by the INT30-C finding on this same line)

ip.ip_len is never validated >= sizeof(ip) before `ntohs(ip.ip_len) - sizeof(ip)`; if a received test frame's IP header claims a length below 20 bytes this size_t subtraction wraps to a huge value, driving the following `for (i=0; i<wrapped;i++) { ...; pos++; }` far out of the 'buf' bounds - genuine integer-underflow-to-OOB-read bug, unlike the other 'earlier-guard' FP family entries which do have a validating check

'pos' is assigned from `&buf[sizeof(*eth)+sizeof(ip)]`, i.e. legitimately derived from indexing into the array-like 'buf' parameter - rule doesn't recognize buffer-index-derived pointers as array pointers
wpa_msg args are MAC2STR(eth->ether_dhost/ether_shost), pure side-effect-free macro reads - matches confirmed EXP30-C macro-logging-arg FP pattern
enabled = atoi(cmd) unchecked, no subsequent validation of the parsed value itself (only truthiness branches on it)
'cmd' is a `char *` pointer parameter to atoi(), not a scalar char being widened - rule appears to misapply the char-widening check to a pointer argument

'cmd' is only read via a local `pos = cmd;` alias in this function, never mutated or forwarded to a non-const call - genuine (low-severity) const opportunity, consistent with the 'plain internal helper, not automatically FP' DCL13-C clarification
`u8 buf[2 + HWSIM_PACKETLEN]` is a fixed-size array sized by a compile-time #define, not a VLA - matches confirmed ENV01-C/MEM05-C fixed-macro-size-array FP pattern

val = strtol(pos,&pos2,0) is immediately range-checked (`val<0||val>0xff` -> return -1), which also catches any LONG_MAX/LONG_MIN overflow result - matches confirmed 'ERR* immediately range-checked' FP pattern extended to strtol

same - the following range check already rejects any overflow-driven strtol result
